item.title: Neko Health CEO: Using AI Scans & Longitudinal Data for a Longer Life
item.description: The CEO of full-body scanner Neko Health says technology could help shift healthcare from treating symptoms to identifying risks earlier. Hjalmar Nilsonne explains how Neko’s scans combine imaging, cardiovascular testing and blood analysis to build a detailed picture of a person’s health, while repeated scans can create longitudinal data to track changes and uncover deeper patterns over time. Nilsonne predicts that in his lifetime AI and more personalized medicine could ultimately help people stay healthier for longer. He spoke to Tom Mackenzie on the latest episode of "Bloomberg Tech: Europe." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DBS Lawsuit Linked to Jho Low’s Associate, Says 1MDB Taskforce
item.description: A lawsuit filed against DBS Group Holdings Ltd. in Singapore’s High Court is related to an associate of Jho Low, the alleged mastermind behind the multi-billion dollar 1Malaysia Development Bhd. scandal, according to the 1MDB Asset Recovery Taskforce.
item.dc:creator: Chanyaporn Chanjaroen

item.title: What’s the Cost of the Premier League’s Global Success?
item.description:
The Premier League has become a global phenomenon — but at what cost?
Adam Blenford explains why some fans are feeling pushed out. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bridgewater's Greg Jensen on AI and the Risk to Humans
item.description: Greg Jensen likens this moment to February 2020.
item.dc:creator: Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal

item.title: Ukraine Strikes Degrade Russian Oil-Refining Industry, IEA Says
item.description: Russia’s oil-processing is being degraded as sanctions prevent the refining industry from recovering from more intense and precise Ukrainian drone strikes, according to the International Energy Agency.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Odd Lots: Bridgewater’s Jensen on AI’s Extinction Risk (Podcast)
item.description: Greg Jensen was one of the earliest backers of both OpenAI and Anthropic, and at Bridgewater Associates, where he is the managing chief investment officer, he leads the hedge fund’s AI strategy. As an early adopter of the technology, he has a lot of thoughts on where things stand right now in terms of model capability and safety, as well as the broader economic impacts of AI. item.title: Oil Price Move Matters More Than CPI: 3-Minutes MLIV
item.description: Anna Edwards, Guy Johnson, Tom Mackenzie and Mark Cudmore break down today's key themes for analysts and investors on "Bloomberg: The Opening Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oura CMO Says Wearable Health Tracking Moving Beyond Checkups
item.description: Oura's Chief Medical Officer suggests wearable tech could give people a continuous picture of their health, rather than relying on occasional doctor visits. Dr. Ricky Bloomfield says the constant stream of health data provided to users of wearables, like Oura's smart rings, can improve health outcomes and influence behavior. He says the long-term goal is to help spot changes earlier and connect people with care sooner. Bloomfield spoke to Tom Mackenzie on the latest episode of "Bloomberg Tech: Europe." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What Standard Blood Pressure Cuffs Miss. Hilo CEO on Continuous Monitoring
item.description: The CEO of Swiss health-tech company Hilo says continuous blood pressure monitoring can reveal patterns that traditional cuff readings may miss. Stefan Petzinger points to night-time changes as particularly important and says Hilo’s software is designed to turn sensor data into useful blood pressure insights. Petzinger also says greater engagement with the data can encourage healthier behavior and better outcomes. He spoke to Tom Mackenzie on the latest episode of "Bloomberg Tech: Europe." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: BNP Paribas Says Warsh Can Prove Credibility With Rate Hike
item.description: Camille de Courcel, head of developed markets rates strategy at BNP Paribas, discusses the outlook for Treasury yields ahead of today's US inflation data and next week's Federal Reserve decision. "I think he's [Fed Chair Kevin Warsh] seen that the July FOMC meeting did not look credible enough for the market," de Courcel tells Bloomberg Television. "He really sees that window of opportunity to show credible and suggest that there will be hikes. So if you don't deliver on that, you can run into a a vicious circle." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Diesel Prices Rise Past $6 a Gallon for First Time Ever
item.description: Diesel prices rose above $6 a gallon for the first time ever, raising the risk of further energy-driven inflation just ahead of peak demand season for the fuel.
item.dc:creator: Will Kubzansky

item.title: Troubled Indonesian Builder Restructures $1 Billion Bank Loans
item.description: Indonesian builder PT PP will restructure 18.2 trillion rupiah ($1 billion) of bank loans, adding to sovereign wealth fund Danantara’s mounting burden of cleaning up troubled state-owned companies.
item.dc:creator: Norman Harsono

item.title: Malaysia’s Zahid Pushes Anwar for Early Election as UMNO Plots Return to Power
item.description: Malaysia’s United Malays National Organisation has called for immediate national elections, signaling deepening tensions within Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s ruling alliance.
item.dc:creator: Kok Leong Chan and Ram Anand

item.title: South African Boards Court Investors as Pay Votes Become Binding
item.description: South African firms are courting shareholders ahead of annual general meetings after new laws gave investors more power over executive pay and put the directors who oversee it under greater pressure.
item.dc:creator: Janice Kew

item.title: Europe Gas Set for Biggest Weekly Gain Since July as War Expands
item.description: European natural gas prices headed for their biggest weekly gain since July as the conflict in the Middle East intensified, stoking fears of deeper and longer energy supply disruptions.
item.dc:creator: Priscila Azevedo Rocha

item.title: DeepSeek Tests SK Hynix Bulls With Fresh Doubts on Memory Demand
item.description: Fund managers wading back into South Korean memory makers’ stocks got a fresh gut check after DeepSeek’s latest artificial intelligence model raised doubts on the strength of demand.
item.dc:creator: Youkyung Lee

item.title: Hitachi, Platinum Are Said Among Bidders for Swarco Unit
item.description: An arm of Hitachi Ltd. is among suitors bidding for part of Swarco, the traffic solutions provider owned by members of Austria’s Swarovski family, people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Eyk Henning and Manuel Baigorri

item.title: Copper Heads for Weekly Loss as Doubts on US Tariffs Intensify
item.description: Copper headed for its first weekly loss since June on concern the US is pushing back a decision on whether to impose import tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Eddie Spence

item.title: Bearish Bets Build in Short India Bonds as Cash Drain Looms
item.description: Bets against India’s short-term bonds are rising, with traders wagering that yields will go up on the central bank’s efforts to drain excess cash from the banking system.
item.dc:creator: Pratigya Vajpayee and Bhaskar Dutta

item.title: Stocks and Treasuries Find Relief Before CPI Print: Markets Wrap
item.description: US stocks and Treasuries caught some respite as oil prices eased, with traders waiting for the August US inflation report for the clearest signal yet on whether the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates next week.
item.dc:creator: Andre Janse van Vuuren
